findings_triage.cause: Native ElementTree parses six JUnit XML outputs without explicit DTD/entity rejection or a file-size/type bound.
findings_triage.trust_boundary: Locally generated pytest outputs enter the release-qualification collector as evidence. They are not remote user uploads, but should remain data.
findings_triage.exploit_assessment: No external-entity file/network exfiltration demonstrated. The rule overstates that behavior for ordinary ElementTree. Untrusted/malformed XML and parser resource limits still merit explicit fail-closed handling.
findings_triage.recommended_disposition: Use bounded regular no-symlink input and defusedxml ElementTree with DTD/entities/external forbidden. Keep all existing nonempty/no-failure/no-error/no-skip requirements; ensure actual collector QA environment has the hash-locked dependency.

findings_triage.cause: Wheel payload source membership compares a recomputed Git SHA1 blob ID with ls-tree metadata; the public-wheel SHA256 and emitted inventory SHA256 do not independently compare accepted source bytes.
findings_triage.trust_boundary: Actual public wheel payload must match the accepted committed source, including non-Python bodies.
findings_triage.exploit_assessment: No collision exploit demonstrated; passing altered bytes would require a suitable Git-blob collision. Nevertheless direct accepted-source equality is available and stronger.
findings_triage.recommended_disposition: Read each accepted Git blob at exact repo+commit/path and require byte equality (or SHA256 against those separately read bytes). Keep all complete-body checks, inventory SHA256 and Git OID/mode protocol metadata. Never replace Git SHA1 IDs with SHA256 IDs.

findings_triage.cause: Native ElementTree reads the three freshly generated installed API/browser/crash JUnit outputs without explicit DTD/entity rejection or bounded regular input.
findings_triage.trust_boundary: Configured isolated pytest processes write evidence which the parent acceptance verifier parses.
findings_triage.exploit_assessment: No remote XML source or demonstrated XXE exfiltration. The evidence-ingestion boundary should nevertheless refuse malformed/DTD/entity-bearing or oversized input.
findings_triage.recommended_disposition: Use bounded regular no-symlink input and defusedxml with DTD/entities/external forbidden, preserving all testcase/failure/error/skip checks. defusedxml0.7.1 is already in existing dev/CPU locks; fresh postpublication bootstrap must actually provide it.

findings_triage.cause: Enterprise evidence: working bytes also match row.sha256; its manifest is separately pinned. SHA1 computes the existing Git object protocol identity.
findings_triage.trust_boundary: Pinned manifest content, regular current worktree bytes and committed HEAD Git identity/mode must agree.
findings_triage.exploit_assessment: A SHA1 collision alone cannot defeat the separate pinned SHA256 body test. HEAD OID relations still rely on Git object semantics; do not describe worktree SHA256 as a separate SHA256 hash of read HEAD bytes.
findings_triage.recommended_disposition: Do not apply SHA1-to-SHA256 autofix or hide/relocate the operation. Legitimate strengthening: compare actual accepted HEAD blob bytes with the pinned current body, retain exact Git metadata and SHA256 checks. Then manual SHA1 recomputation is unnecessary. Relevant independent SHA256 check is at line 435.

findings_triage.cause: Argparse output path flows to build --no-isolation --outdir <absolute output>, run in the exact committed source extracted from git archive. The command is a literal argv list; no shell=True, string shell command, eval or executable selected by this path.
findings_triage.trust_boundary: Operator/CI packaging output selection; source backend execution is intentional for reviewed source. Output is Path.resolve() absolute at line564 and created fresh at578.
findings_triage.exploit_assessment: No shell injection path established. Metacharacters remain literal path characters; absolute filenames cannot become leading option flags. A hostile accepted build backend or poisoned Python module environment is a different prerequisite, not this path-taint result.
findings_triage.recommended_disposition: Do not add shlex.quote to argv values or weaken official rules. Preserve required audit finding and context. Optional real hardening is isolated -I for trusted Python build/twine frontend lookup; it does not turn arbitrary source-backend execution into a safe sandbox.

findings_triage.cause: Creates a Git-format blob OID for fixed inert Python fixture bytes to mock ls-tree source identities.
findings_triage.trust_boundary: Synthetic test data and mocked Git responses; no production security authentication.
findings_triage.exploit_assessment: No attacker-controlled digest or production trust grant established. The expected hash is Git protocol data.
findings_triage.recommended_disposition: Keep fixture Git semantics. If removing manual hashing, construct real fixture objects through the existing isolated Git fixture machinery or actual git hash-object; do not swap hash algorithms or disguise the same hashlib call to evade a rule.

findings_triage.cause: PRE_COMMIT_HOME selects a cache glob and the fixture executes each candidate Python before accepting its Semgrep version. Probe lacks -I.
findings_triage.trust_boundary: An operator-controlled tool/cache location is being treated as an interpreter authority; it is not website/mission input.
findings_triage.exploit_assessment: Executing a forged probe requires control of PRE_COMMIT_HOME or writable selected cache entries. No remote exploit or shell metacharacter injection demonstrated. A malicious executable could run before its printed version is checked; -I also closes current-directory/user-site/PYTHON* influence, but does not authenticate an arbitrary executable.
findings_triage.recommended_disposition: Isolate the probe with -I and bind discovery to an explicitly trusted qualified tool environment/cache origin, or run tests using an already qualified pinned interpreter. Version text alone is not executable provenance. Fail closed for unknown origins; preserve custom-cache behavior only inside an explicit trusted configuration.

findings_triage.cause: Constructs matching SHA256 and Git OID metadata for deliberately invalid synthetic media. The regression requires media rejection despite matching hashes.
findings_triage.trust_boundary: Inert local fixture generation, not production evidence authentication.
findings_triage.exploit_assessment: No security digest or production authority grant established; the test is specifically an adversarial refusal case.
findings_triage.recommended_disposition: Preserve exact Git fixture identity and negative media test. Actual isolated Git object construction is an honest alternative if manual hash reproduction is removed; no SHA256 substitution for Git OIDs or scanner suppression.
